newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Gateway says it first with Pentium 2.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Gateway says it first with Pentium 2.

text.p: By Neil Winton, Science and Technology Correspondent
Gateway 2000 Inc, which sells personal computers by mail order, said it expects to gain market share in Europe by being the first to incorporate Intel Corp's new Pentium 2 chip in its PCs.
Intel of the U.S. launches the Pentium 2 this week.

"We believe that our PCs will be available in Europe with the new Pentium 2 chip between 30 and 60 days before it appears in retail outlets," Paul Collas, Gateway's senior product manager said in a telephone interview.

Gateway sells PCs direct to the customer, and says it designs each one individually. Because this cuts stocks and avoids retail markups, prices are often the keenest available, according to the North Sioux City, South Dakota based company.

"We will have the advantage to grab market share in Europe, and we plan to be number one of Pentium 2 systems in Europe. We feel sure we can attain that," Collas said in a telephone interview from Gateway's Dublin, Ireland, European headquarters.
Analysts agreed that the Pentium 2 move would enhance market share for Gateway, but pointed out the narrow nature of the company's sales.
"Gateway targets a very specific section of the market - consumers that have money, that need a PC to work or play," said Emmanuel Lalloz, senior PC research analyst at CONTEXT.

"Gateway customers are often computer freaks, they like it for its own sake. This will certainly give Gateway an edge in that segment of the consumer market which focuses on the technology," Lalloz said.
"The Pentium 2 is not really a consumer chip. It really is to replace the Pentium Pro, for high end needs like graphics," Lalloz said.
Gateway's Collas said the Pentium 2 chip will enhance PC performance dramatically and that the advantage over other systems would last at least two years.

"The great thing about Pentium 2 is that it eliminates the decision for the high end customer on what product to invest in. It decodes software video and audio clips much quicker, and brings multimedia to the next level. It enhances video and audio output of PCs."

"It just runs all the software much quicker. It really is the optimum platform. If you use graphics it delivers raw horse power. Pentium 2 will be able to take advantage of software programes written in one to two years time," Collas said.
Last year Gateway raised its sales in Europe by just over 40 percent to 250,000. About 90 percent of its sales were desk-top personal computers, with the remainder portables.

Its customers tend to be computer enthusiasts and analysts say that with this section of the market becoming saturated, Gateway must soon turn its attention to markets like the small office, home office, and eventually the mass market.
